Subject: Renewal timing and billing alignment for DataWave (DW-042)

Hi Sofia —

Hope you’re well. Our finance team has asked us to consolidate renewals across our analytics portfolio to a single fiscal-window (Oct 1 start). We’re coming up on the renewal for the Redwood contract (current term expires 2025-11-30) and want to understand options for aligning to Oct 1 without losing committed capacity, and to stage a capacity uplift across Q4–Q1 to support a new feature launch.

Key asks:
- Can we co-term to Oct 1, 2026 and convert the current remaining months into pro-rated credits?
- What does a staged uplift (20% additional capacity in month 1, then +30% month 4) look like pricing-wise on a 24-month term vs 12-month?
- Any auto-renew implications we need to opt-out of?

If it helps, happy to do a quick call — procurement (Priya Rao) will join.

Thanks —
Sam
Director, Platform Engineering
DataWave Analytics

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal timing and billing alignment for DataWave (DW-042)

Sam —

Thank you — this is doable and we have three pragmatic paths that commonly work for customers wanting fiscal alignment plus staged capacity:

1) Short co-term + prorated credit (best for preserving pricing flexibility)
   - Co-term to Oct 1, 2026 by issuing a prorated credit for the 2 months remaining on the current term (Dec and Jan pro-rated).
   - Maintain 12-month cadence thereafter; staged uplift billed as monthly true-up.

2) 24-month staircase (best $/token economics + predictability)
   - Move to a 24-month agreement starting Oct 1, 2025 with an initial committed baseline and scheduled step-ups (20% at T0+30 days, +30% at T0+120 days).
   - We can offer structured discounting on the stepped amounts and a small onboarding credit to cover migration risk.

3) Hybrid co-term + annualized overlay (best for procurement that wants longer visibility without full commitment)
   - Co-term to Oct 1 and convert remaining months into a short bridge credit; set a 12-month committed baseline for Year 1 and optionally annualize Year 2 with a capped uplift floor.

Auto-renew: all options allow the standard auto-renew clause, but we can add explicit opt-out windows in the SOW so Proc has time to decide before renewal.

I’ve attached a short scenario workbook and a draft mutual action plan. Marissa — can you confirm typical discount bands for staged uplift on a 24-month? Karthik — any constraints from legal/finance on co-term credits being issued as invoice credits vs prepaid adjustments?

If it works, I can book a 30-minute call with you + Priya + procurement for Monday 18th.

Best,
Sofia
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

(Attachments: DW_Renewal_Scenarios_v2.pdf, Mutual_Action_Plan_DW-042.xlsx)

Quick notes on pricing bands — from RevOps perspective:

- 12-month: uplift billed at list + 12–18% (monthly true-up); no onboarding credit.
- 24-month staircase: step credits possible, effective uplift on stepped volumes = list - 8–14% depending on committed mix.
- If they commit to a minimum aggregate spend over 24 months (we can structure as convertible credits), we can push discount to -16% on the stepped increments.

Also recommend structuring the billing cutover as:
- Oct 1 start date for new term (co-terming).
- Issue invoice credit for unused days in current term (finance prefers credits on the next invoice to avoid reversal).

Sofia — I'll draft a short pricing table and give you two named playbooks (24mo_stage and co-term_bridge) you can send into procurement.

Marissa
Director, Renewal & Expansion | Redwood Inference
